TextView.android:text: Wombat Liberates needs Android Accessibility access so it can read the Kindle page currently on screen. When Android opens Accessibility settings, scroll down to Wombat Liberates, tap it, then turn on Allow.

Tap Start Kindle scan, then open Kindle at the first page you want. The scan stops by itself at the end of the book. If a scan stopped early, tap Start Kindle scan again and choose Continue scan. To check everything works first, run a short Test scan from Advanced settings. You can also import an existing text file instead.

Kindle must stay open and visible on your screen for the entire scan. Wombat Liberates reads each Kindle page as it appears; switching to another app, locking the phone, or using the phone for something else interrupts the scan.

Each screen takes about 1.5 seconds, so a long book can take 30 minutes or more. Connect your phone to power and leave Kindle on screen. If Kindle will not turn a page, or a page looks like a table, the phone buzzes and a small panel asks what to do. Set Pages with tables to Keep or Skip in Advanced settings for unattended scans.

When a scan finishes, the review screen opens. Text is cleaned on your phone automatically, including removing Kindle footer text, and given a quality rating. View, compare and save any version as text or EPUB. Only if the rating says the OCR is poor, set up Ollama under Advanced settings and tap Clean with Ollama on the review screen, then compare its changes before using it. Raw OCR is never changed.

Enter a title and author, then create an EPUB. It uses the version chosen in Review (device cleanup unless you pick another). Headings such as CHAPTER SIX become entries in the table of contents. Open in EPUB reader on the review screen sends a book straight to your reader app.
Screenshots are OCRed locally and discarded. Text remains on your phone unless you choose Ollama cleanup, which sends text only to the server you configure.
